text:
JT 1094

SUPERIOR COURT

CANADA

PROVINCE OF QUEBEC

DISTRICT OF

MONTREAL

No:

500-17-013166-023

DATE:

May 31, 2004

______________________________________________________________________

By:

THE HONOURABLE MADAM JUSTICE ANNE-MARIE
TRAHAN, J.S.C.

______________________________________________________________________

SMBD – JEWISH GENERAL
HOSPITAL

Plaintiff

vs.

MARTHA KUMMERMANN

and

HANNA SARAFFIAN

Defendants

______________________________________________________________________

JUDGMENT

______________________________________________________________________

[
1
]

The Plaintiff (J.G.H.) claims $29,466.29 from
the Defendants, Madam Kummermannn and her daughter Madam Saraffian (who
administers her mother's property).  This amount represents the fees which are
due for the long term care lodging provided to Madam Kummermann by the J.G.H.
since December 8, 2000, until now.  The J.G.H. asks that the Defendants be
asked to pay the cost of Madam Kummermann's lodging as long as she remains in
its establishement.

[
2
]

The J.G.H. also asks that Madam Saraffian be
condemned to pay said amount as administrator of her mother's property.  It
asks that she be condemned because she is not acting in her mother's best
interests, which is her obligation as administrator of her mother's property.

[
3
]

In the Cross-Demand she filed, on her behalf and
on behalf of her mother, Madam Saraffian claims $590,000.00 for her mother and
$400,000.00 for herself.  For the reasons given in the judgment dated April 14,
2004, the undersigned struck the Defence and the Cross-Demand on behalf of
Madam Kummermann.  We are therefore left with Madam Saraffian's claims for
harassment ($200,000) and for loss of income ($200,000).

[
4
]

During the hearing, the J.G.H. presented a
Motion to have Madam Saraffian declared a vexatious litigant (the Rules of
Practice now talk about quarrelsome conduct).

[
5
]

I.
THE CLAIM FOR $29,466.29
AGAINST MADAM KUMMERMANN

[
6
]

Pursuant to the decision rendered by the
undersigned on April 14, 2004, the case is proceeding by default against Madam
Kummermann.  Madam Kummermann has been a long term care patient at the J.G.H.
since December 8, 2000.

[
7
]

The «
Loi sur les services de santé et les
services sociaux
»
[1]
states the conditions under which such lodging takes place.  Articles 512, 513 and 514 read as follows:

512.
Le gouvernement détermine, par
règlement, la contribution qui peut être exigée des usagers qui sont hébergés
dans une installation maintenue par un établissement public ou privé
conventionné ou qui sont pris en charge par une ressource intermédiaire d'un
établissement public ou par une ressource de type fam
ilial.

Dépenses personnelles

Ce règlement détermine également le montant d'allocation de dépenses
personnelles qui doit être laissé mensuellement à cet usager.

Montant

513.
Le montant de la
contribution peut varier suivant les circonstances ou les besoins identifiés
par règlement.

Usagers visés

La contribution est exigée par un établissement ou par le ministre.
Les usagers eux-mêmes sont tenus de la verser; toutefois, dans le cas d'un usager
mineur, la contribution peut être exigée de son père, de sa mère, de l'un et
l'autre conjointement ou de toute autre personne déterminée par le règlement;
dans le cas d'un usager marié ou uni civilement, la contribution peut être exigée
de son conjoint et dans le cas d'un membre d'une communauté religieuse, la
contribution peut être exigée de sa communauté.

Exonération

514.
Le ministre ou un
établissement désigné par règlement peut, à la demande d'une personne de qui
est exigé le paiement d'une contribution, l'exonérer du paiement de cette
contribution, selon les modalités et dans les circonstances déterminées par
règlement.

512.
The Government shall
determine, by regulation, the contribution that may be required of users
lodged in a facility maintained by a public or private institution under agreement,
or taken in charge by an intermediate resource of a public institution or by
a family-type resource.

Personal allowance.

The regulation shall also determine
the amount of personal expense allowance which must be left at the disposal
of the user each month.

Amount of contribution.

513.
The amount of the
contribution may vary according to the circumstances or needs identified by
regulation.

Payment.

The contribution shall be
required by an institution or by the Minister. The users themselves are bound
to pay it; however, in the case of a user who is a minor, the contribution
may be required of the user's father, mother, both of them jointly or any
other person determined by regulation; in the case of a user who is married
or in a civil union, the contribution may be required of the spouse and, in
the case of a member of a religious community, the contribution may be required
of the community.

Exemption.

514.
The Minister or an
institution designated by regulation may, at the request of a person of whom
payment of a contribution is required, exempt such person from paying the
contribution, in accordance with the terms and conditions and in the
circumstances determined by regulation.

[
8
]

The Act talks about:  "a user
lodged".  Madam Kummermann is such a person.

[
9
]

These provisions impose on the patient a legal
obligation to pay the accommodation contribution established by the Regulation.
[2]

[
10
]

After Madam Kummermann was admitted to the
J.G.H., Madam Saraffian requested an exoneration of the accommodation
contribution charged to her mother.  She invoked the fact that Madam Kummermann
has a debt of over $22,000.00 U.S. (the amount of the burial fees and related
expenses for her first daughter who passed away in the United States).  She
also invoked the fact that Madam Kummermann was not well treated by the J.G.H.

[
11
]

The «
Direction de la contribution et de
l'aide financières
» of the «
Régie de l'assurance-maladie du Québec
»
rendered its decision on January 24, 2001 and reduced the monthly accomodation
contribution to $783.38.  On March 12, 2001, Madam Saraffian applied for a
review of said decision on behalf of her mother.  On April 17, 2001   (P-4),
the application for review was denied.  Subsequently, Madam Kummermann, through
her daughter, appealed the decision (P-4) to the «
Tribunal administratif du
Québec
».  A decision was rendered on January 22, 2003, confirming the
decision of the «
Régie de l'assurance-maladie du Québec
».  Madam
Kummermann then requested, once again through her daughter, that this decision
be revised by the «
Tribunal administratif du Québec
».  The decision on
the application for revision was rendered on September 4, 2003 and the revision
was refused (P-5).  Hence the decision of the «
Régie de l'assurance-maladie
du Québec
» stands and Madam Kummermann owes $783.38 a month.  Madam
Saraffian has mentioned, during the hearing, she was considering filing a
Motion for judicial review:  it can be filed within a reasonable delay, says
she.

[
12
]

Exhibits P-1, P-1A, P-1B and P-1C are the
statements of account of the J.G.H. and show that Madam Kummermann owes the sum
of $29,466.96 as of April 2004.  Since the amount claimed in the Plaintiff's
action is $29,466.29, this is the amount which will be allowed.

[
13
]

II.
THE REQUEST FOR PAYMENT OF THE
AMOUNTS WHICH WILL BECOME DUE AS LONG AS MADAM KUMMERMANN REMAINS HOSPITALIZED

[
14
]

In its Amended Declaration of April 6, 2004, the
Plaintiff claims it is entitled to ask that Madam Kummermann be ordered to pay
the amounts that will become due as long as she remains lodged as a long term
care patient at the J.G.H., since the monthly amount is established by
Regulation and by the «
Régie
» and is therefore certain.

[
15
]

Plaintiff invokes article 1611 C.C.Q. which
reads as follows:

Les dommages-intérêts
dus au créancier compensent la perte qu'il subit et le gain dont il est
privé.

On tient
compte, pour les dé-terminer, du préjudice futur lorsqu'il est certain et
qu'il est susceptible d'être évalué.

The damages
due to the creditor compensate for the amount of the loss he has sustained
and the profit of which he has been deprived.

Future injury which is certain and able to be assessed is taken into
account in awarding damages.

[
16
]

In their treaty entitled «
Les obligations
»
[3]
,
Jean-Louis Baudouin and Pierre-Gabriel Jobin write:

829 – Préjudice
certain –
En
matière contractuelle comme en matière extracontractuelle, le préjudice, qu'il
soit présent ou futur, doit être certain pour pouvoir être réparé
[4]
.  Cette condition soulève des problèmes
pratiques, spécialement pour le préjudice futur.  Celui-ci peut être compensé
mais la personne qui en réclame compensation doit démontrer la probabilité de
sa réalisation dans l'avenir
[5]
.  Il n'est pas nécessaire que le préjudice futur soit
certain dans un sens absolu, du moment qu'il n'est pas seulement hypothétique
ou éventuel
[6]
.

Par ailleurs, le préjudice doit aussi être
susceptible d'être évalué au moment où le tribunal doit le liquider.  Les
tribunaux exigent en général que le créancier prouve le manque réel des profits
réclamés et n'accordent donc pas d'indemnisation pour des profits incertains ou
trop aléatoires
[7]
.  Par contre, il est bien établi que les tribunaux,
dans l'appréciation des dommages futurs, doivent prendre en considération les
événements intervenus entre la date de l'inexécution et celle où l'action a été
prise, de même que les faits nouveaux survenus depuis l'inexécution
[8]
, sous réserve des restrictions, déjà
signalées, sur la cascade de préjudices
[9]
.
[10]

[
17
]

In the present matter, there is no doubt that,
as long as Madam Kummermann is lodged at the J.G.H., she will have to pay
$783.38 a month.  A statement for this amount is sent each month by «
la
Régie de l'assurance-maladie du Québec
» to the J.G.H.  Therefore, the
amount of damages is certain and able to be assessed in accordance with the
terms of article 1611 C.P.C.

[
18
]

Article 4.2 C.P.C. reads as follows:

4.2.
Dans toute instance, les parties doivent s'assurer
que les actes de procédure choisis sont, eu égard aux coûts et au temps
exigés, proportionnés à la nature et à la finalité de la demande et à la
complexité du litige; le juge doit faire de même à l'égard des actes de
procédure qu'il autorise ou ordonne.

4.2.
In any proceeding, the parties must ensure
that the proceedings they choose are proportionate, in terms of the costs and

time required, to the
nature and ultimate purpose of the action or application and to the
complexity of the dispute; the same applies to proceedings authorized or ordered
by the judge.

[
19
]

The Court also takes into consideration the fact
that the trial, in the present case, has taken seven days whereas it was
scheduled for three.  It also takes into consideration the costs involved with
any trial, the time required, the nature and ultimate purpose of the action
Plaintiff would have to take in order to claim the amounts which will accrue
monthly as long as Madam Kummermann is in the J.G.H.  Finally, the Court takes
into account the best interests of the Administration of Justice.  This is why
the Court is of the opinion that the request for an order for future damages is
justified.

[
20
]

III.
THE CLAIMS AGAINST MADAM
SARAFFIAN PERSONNALLY AND AS ADMINISTRATOR

[
21
]

A.         AS ADMINISTRATOR

[
22
]

On the first day of the trial, Madam Sarrafian
invoked the fact that Madam Kummermann gave her a Power of Attorney entitled:
"Durable General Power of Attorney" (D-34).  It is dated July
29, 1998 and was signed in New York.  It allows Madam Saraffian to administer
Madam Kummermann's property.  Madam Saraffian recognizes that she acts under
the terms of this Power of Attorney.  She never contested its validity nor has
Plaintiff.

[
23
]

The Court is, therefore, of the opinion that
Madam Saraffian is charged with the administration of property that is not her
own.

[
24
]

As administrator, Madam Saraffian is governed by

Title
Seven
"
Administration of
the Property of Others
" of
Book
Four
"
Property
"
of the
Civil Code of Quebec
.

[
25
]

Articles 1299, 1308, 1309, 1310 and 1345 C.C.Q.
read as follows:

1299.
Toute personne qui est chargée d'administrer
un bien ou un patrimoine qui n'est pas le sien assume la charge
d'administrateur du bien d'autrui. Les règles du présent titre s'appliquent à
une administration, à moins qu'il ne résulte de la loi, de l'acte constitutif
ou des circonstances qu'un autre régime d'administration ne soit applicable.

1299.
Any person who is charged with the
administration of property or a patrimony that is not his own assumes the
office of administrator of the property of others. The rules of this Title
apply to every administration unless another form of administration applies
under the law or the constituting act, or due to circumstances.

1308.
L'administrateur du bien d'autrui
doit, dans l'exercice de ses fonctions, respecter les obligations que la loi
et l'acte constitutif lui imposent; il doit agir dans les limites des
pouvoirs qui lui sont conférés.

Il ne répond pas de la perte du bien qui
résulte d'une force majeure, de la vétusté du bien, de son dépérissement ou
de l'usage normal et autorisé du bien.

1308.
The administrator of the property
of others shall, in carrying out his duties, comply with the obligations
imposed on him by law or by the constituting act. He shall act within the
powers conferred on him.

He is not liable for loss of the property resulting from a superior
force or from its age, its perishable nature or its normal and authorized
use.

1309.
L'administrateur doit agir avec
prudence et diligence.

Il doit aussi agir avec honnêteté et
loyauté, dans le meilleur intérêt du bénéficiaire ou de la fin poursuivie.

1309.
An administrator shall act with
prudence and diligence.

He shall also act honestly and faithfully in the
best interest of the beneficiary or of the object pursued.

1310.
L'administrateur ne peut exercer
ses pouvoirs dans son propre intérêt ni dans celui d'un tiers; il ne peut non
plus se placer dans une situation de conflit entre son intérêt personnel et
ses obligations d'administrateur.

S'il est lui-même bénéficiaire, il doit
exercer ses pouvoirs dans l'intérêt commun, en considérant son intérêt au
même titre que celui des autres bénéficiaires.

1310.
No administrator may exercise his
powers in his own interest or that of a third person or place himself in a
position where his personal interest is in conflict with his obligations as
administrator.

If the administrator himself is a beneficiary, he
shall exercise his powers in the common interest, giving the same
consideration to his own interest as to that of the other beneficiaries.

1345.
La répartition des bénéfices et des
dépenses, entre le bénéficiaire des fruits et revenus et celui du capital, se
fait conformément aux dispositions de l'acte constitutif et suivant
l'intention qui y est manifestée.

À défaut
d'indication suffisante dans l'acte, cette répartition se fait le plus
équitablement possible, en tenant compte de l'objet de l'administration, des
circonstances qui y ont donné lieu et des usages comptables généralement
reconnus.

1345.
Apportionment of profit and
expenditure between the beneficiary of the fruits and revenues and the
beneficiary of the capital is made in accordance with the stipulations and
clear intention of the constituting act.

Failing sufficient indication in the act, apportionment is made as
equitably as possible, taking into account the object of the administration,
the circumstances that gave rise to it and generally recognized accounting
practices.

[
26
]

As administrator, Madam Saraffian has the
obligation to pay the debts of Madam Kummermann.  Therefore, she is liable, in
her capacity as administrator, for the payment of the amounts owed by Madam
Kummermann, i.e.:  the sum of $29,466.29 up to April 2004, as well as
the amount of $783.38 a month which will accrue subsequently as long as Madam
Kummermann is lodged.

[
27
]

B.
PERSONNALLY

[
28
]

Plaintiff invokes article 1626, 1627 and 1628
C.C.Q. and purports to exercise the rights and actions belonging to Madam
Kummermann, who is its debtor, against Madam Saraffian.  Plaintiff alleges
Madam Saraffian is Madam Kummermann's debtor because, as administrator, she
does not act in the best interests of her mother, thereby causing her damages.

1626.
Le créancier peut prendre toutes
les mesures nécessaires ou utiles à la conservation de ses droits.

1626.
A creditor may take all necessary
or useful measures to preserve his rights.

1627.
Le créancier dont la créance est
certaine, liquide et exigible peut, au nom de son débiteur, exercer les
droits et actions de celui-ci, lorsque le débiteur, au préjudice du
créancier, refuse ou néglige de les exercer.

Il ne peut, toutefois, exercer les droits et actions qui sont
exclusivement attachés à la personne du
débiteur.

1627.
A creditor whose claim is certain,
liquid and exigible may exercise the rights and actions belonging to the
debtor, in the debtor's name, where the debtor refuses or neglects to
exercise them to the prejudice of the creditor.

However, he may not exercise rights and actions which are strictly
personal to the debtor.

1628.
Il n'est pas nécessaire que la créance soit
liquide et exigible au moment où l'action est intentée; mais elle doit l'être
au moment du jugement sur l'action.

1628.
It is not necessary for the claim
to be liquid and exigible at the time the action is instituted, but it is
necessary that it be so at the time judgment is rendered.

[
29
]

The J.G.H. believes it would be in Madam
Kummermann's best interests to be transferred to a long term care facility and
claims that the transfer does not take place because of Madam Saraffian's
actions.

[
30
]

Madam Saraffian does not pay the prescribed
contribution for Madam Kummermann's lodging at the J.G.H.  The evidence shows
that she has also said she would not pay such contribution if her mother were
transferred to a specialized long term care facility.  Because of this refusal
and because of Madam Saraffian's behaviour toward the staff of a rehabilitation
hospital (Julius Richardson) where her mother was hospitalized and which is
connected with a long term care hospital (Henri Bradet), the management of
Henri Bradet has refused to accept her mother.  The «
Régie
» has asked
her to solve the problem of her paying the fees before agreeing to place her
mother elsewhere, where she would receive more appropriate care.  According to
Madam Iorio, the J.G.H. social worker involved in the case, Madam Kummermann's
quality of life would improve with the stimulation and other care she would
receive in a specialized facility.

[
31
]

Plaintiff states that it is exercising «
une
action oblique
» whereby it puts itself in the place of Madam Kummermann
who, according to Plaintiff, has a claim against Madam Sarrafian because she is
not acting in Madam Kummermann's best interests which is contrary to her
obligation as an administrator.

[
32
]

The «
action oblique
» is a special type of
procedure which must comply with the rules enunciated in article 1627 C.C.Q. in
order to be allowed.

[
33
]

In the case of
Larocque
vs.
Pilon
[11]
, a doctor was allowed
to exercise, against a husband separated as to bed and board from his wife, the
recourse for alimentary pension that the wife had neglected to exercise against
her husband, in order to recover from the husband the cost of the medical care
provided by the doctor to his wife.  The Court came to the conclusion that the
husband's obligation to pay an alimentary pension to his wife included the
obligation to pay the costs of medical care within the limits of his means and
the needs of his wife.  The medical treatment was required because, without it,
there was a risk of fatal hemorrhages and of the
patient developing a cancer of uterus.

[
34
]

In an another case:
Harris
vs.
Royal
Victoria Hospital
[12]
,
the Royal Victoria Hospital was refused the right to recover its charges for
hospitalization and medical services from the son-in-law of a patient, because
it had failed to allege that the patient was put in default to exercise any
claim she might have had against her son-in-law or that she had refused or neglected
to do so.  The decision of the Court of Appeal is based on article 1031
C.C.B.C. which reads as follows:

Les créanciers peuvent exercer les droits et actions de leur
débiteur, à l'exception de ceux qui sont exclusivement attachés à sa
personne, lorsque, à leur préjudice, il refuse ou néglige de le faire.

Creditors may exercise the rights and actions of
their debtor, when to their prejudice he refuses or neglects to do so;  with
the exception of those rights which are exclusively attached to the person.

[
35
]

Although some modifications were brought by
article 1627 C.C.Q. to article 1031 C.C.B.C., the obligation for the Plaintiff
in an «
action oblique
» to put its own debtor in default to exercise a
right and to prove the existence of a refusal or neglect to exercise such
right, still exists.

[
36
]

In the present case, there is no evidence that
the J.G.H. has ever put Madam Kummermann in default to exercise a recourse in
damages against Madam Saraffian because Madam Saraffian is not acting in Madam
Kummermann's best interests and that, pursuant to such a «
mise en demeure
»,
Madam Kummermann refuses or neglects to act against Madam Saraffian.  This is
why the Court is of the opinion that it cannot grant «
l'action oblique
»
of Plaintiff against Defendant Saraffian.

[
37
]

IV.
DEFENDANT SARAFFIAN'S
CROSS-DEMAND IN THE AMOUNT OF $400,000.00

[
38
]

Madam Saraffian explains her claim in the amount
of $400,000.00 in the last two subparagraphs of paragraph 28 of her Answer to
Amended Declaration and Amended Defence and Cross-Demand of August 8, 2002.
They read as follows:

"Co-Defendant HANNA SARAFFIAN, for being constantly and
persistently viciously harassed by different Medical Professionals consisting
of Doctors and Nurses for the past two years and ongoing by denying her the
right to stay with her mother after 11:00 P.M. and humiliating her by the
constant threats that Security will be called, and or by indiscriminately
calling security to have her removed from her mothers (sic) side.  Stressing
her by rushing her out of her mothers (sic) room and the ward were (sic) she
resides.  Thereby causing horrendous psychological turmoil and psychological
distress.  And to ad (sic) insult to injury staff members have slandered her by
documenting false events or verbally to her face.

$200,000.-

Co-Defendant has lost considerable income from business, because of
the constant harassment by the different staff members of Plaintiff JEWISH
GENERAL HOSPITAL.  Defendant was and is so stressed out from this ordeal that
she often cannot sleep entire nights and is therefore unable to work the
following day.  This has caused her severe financial prejudice.  This situation
with the Hospital in order to protect her mother Defendant MARTHA KUMMERMANN
the ordeal became a full time job for Co-Defendant HANNA SARAFFIAN, which is
demonstrated by the exhibits in this action.

$200,000.-"

[
39
]

As Cross-Plaintiff, Madam Saraffian has the
burden of proving her claim.  She has made her views known quite at length as a
witness, while she was cross-examining witnesses and while addressing the Court
on various points raised throughout the hearing.  A review of the «
procès-verbaux
»
of the hearing indicates that Madam Saraffian was allowed about 31h08 of Court
time for her testimony, her cross-examination and the various witnesses submitted
by the J.G.H. and, above all, for the various representations and pleadings she
submitted to the Court throughout the hearing.  As indicated above, the trial
was scheduled for three days;  it lasted seven!

[
40
]

A.
THE CROSS-DEMAND FOR
HARRASSMENT

[
41
]

In long term care units in hospitals, visitation
hours are not as strict as elsewhere because of the particular nature of such
units.  Usually, visitors are allowed to come and go 24 hours a day.  It is
felt that the presence of loved ones is a good thing for the patients who need
the warmth, affection and tender loving care of family members and friends.  It
also helps them adapt to their new «
milieu de vie
».

[
42
]

The evidence reveals that indeed the J.G.H. has
imposed a "curfew" to Madam Saraffian.  Throughout the years, it has
gone from 11:00 p.m. to 11:30 p.m. and it is now midnight.  According to the
evidence, this measure has been put in place because when she comes to visit
her mother late at night, Madam Saraffian wakes her up and feeds her.  Very
often, Madam Kummermann is lying flat in her bed.  The J.G.H. is worried that
such a practice might be dangerous for Madam Kummermann:  she may
choke while eating lying flat in her bed.  Madam Saraffian replies that, often,
her mother is sitting up in bed.  However, exhibit P-2 which is the complete
hospital file of Madam Kummermann shows that the nurses have written on a
number of occasions that the mother was lying flat in bed while she was being
fed by the daughter.

[
43
]

Madam Kummermann occupies a bed in a double room.
Very often, Madam Saraffian opens the light on her mother's side which disturbs
the other patient.  Madam Saraffian says the curtain is drawn around her
mother's bed and that it is dark on the other patient's side.  The Court has
its doubts about the accuracy of Madam Saraffian statement since the curtain
separating the beds in hospital are far from being heavy drapes preventing the
light to come through.  They do let light go through, especially in their upper
part which is like a net.

[
44
]

The preponderance of the evidence is that Madam
Saraffian has had discussions with the staff in a tone which is far from being
appropriate for that time of the night when most of the patients are sleeping
or trying to sleep.  Madam Saraffian claims she has been provoked by the staff
and that this is why she has raised her voice.  The Court does not believe
Madam Saraffian.  It is a fact that some of the staff members have behaved in
such a way that they have been disciplined by the J.G.H.  However, there are
only two such employees and the head nurse, Madam Kalfon, has testified that
they were not dismissed because of their behaviour towards Madam Saraffian.

[
45
]

Having seen Madam Saraffian's demeanour in the
court room, the type of comments she makes about the staff, about the services
given to her mother, the condition of the premises, etc., the Court is of the
opinion that she is part of the problem, if not the problem itself.

[
46
]

The Court understands the very close and
emotional links between Madam Saraffian and her mother.  The Court has heard
Madam Saraffian say that her mother is everything for her and that she is
everything for her mother.  It is never easy for a daughter to see her mother
age.  The Court is convinced that Madam Saraffian genuinely loves her mother
and wants to give her what she thinks is best for her and wants to complement
what she considers to be not very good care.

[
47
]

However, for the time being, Madam Kummermann is
lodged in a long term care unit in a general hospital and Madam Saraffian
cannot make the rules in such a unit (nor in any other unit for that matter).
She must also recognize that other patients have rights and that it is the role
of the hospital staff to ensure that they are respected.  This is why the Court
does not consider that, by imposing a curfew to Madam Saraffian, the J.G.H. has
harassed her:  it was acting in the best interests of the rest of the
patients and also of Madam Kummermann who needs to sleep at night since there
is a hospital routine to follow during the day.

[
48
]

Madam Saraffian claims that she has established
good relations with some staff members, that she brings them gifts and that she
is appreciated by them.  While the head nurse, Madam Kalfon, recognizes that
Madam Saraffian does bring gifts for some staff members, she does not agree
that they like her and that there is a good relationship between them.

[
49
]

Madam Saraffian produced D-31:  a
photocopy of a notice, written by Madam Kalfon, which was posted inside the
Nursing Station.  It reminds the staff that if Madam Saraffian does not leave
the unit by 11:00 p.m., the staff should call the security and the nursing
coordinator in order that she be escorted out of the hospital.

[
50
]

Madam Saraffian first testified that this note
was posted on the outside window of the Nursing Station and that it was visible
for everyone to see.  Once this was contradicted by Madam Kalfon, who stated it
was posted inside the Nursing Station, Madam Saraffian claimed that, by
transparency, everybody could read it.  However, no patients and no relatives
of patients testified they had seen that document, read it and, because they
had read the notice, they had lost their respect for Madam Saraffian.

[
51
]

Madam Saraffian claims that the various
statements written in the medical file of her mother (P-2) are false, self-serving
and are a fabrication of evidence in favour of those writing such statements.
It is certain that confronted to a person like Madam Saraffian, a staff member
will try and will put his or her version of the facts on the record so that, if
need be, this will serve as evidence in their favour.  It must be pointed out,
however, that such statements are written immediately or very shortly after the
events have taken place and that they are normal hospital procedures.  The
Court is of the opinion they do not constitute a conspiracy against Madam
Saraffian contrary to what she believes.

[
52
]

In the present case, it is understandable that,
in dealing with somebody like Madam Saraffian, the staff wants to make sure
that something is written in the file.

[
53
]

Taking all the evidence into consideration, the
Court is of the opinion that Madam Saraffian has not discharged the burden of
proving that her claim for harassment is well founded.  Therefore, it is
dismissed.

[
54
]

B.
THE CROSS-DEMAND FOR
LOSS OF INCOME

[
55
]

At one point, before this saga started, Madam
Saraffian was working in the steel industry.  It is a specialized and
competitive industry.  Madam Saraffian was in charge of international marketing
for a company.  She also had, at one point, incorporated her own consulting
company of which she is the only shareholder did she tell us.  Madam Saraffian
did not give the Court any specific evidence as to her terms of employment, her
earnings, those of the Company, the value of the Company.  In other words,
there is no evidence as to the financial aspect of the claim for loss of
income.

[
56
]

The evidence reveals that, indeed, Madam
Saraffian devotes a lot of time to her mother.  However, the preponderance of
the evidence is that, contrary to what she states, she is not there every day
or every evening.  When she comes, she brings natural medicine for her mother,
which she gives her.  She brings her food which she gives her.  She claims that
her mother is not well treated because, amongst others,  there has been
problems with her shoes, her food, her dentures, her reading glasses, etc. and
that she has had to spend a lot of time dealing with those problems and has not
been able to work and has, thereby, lost considerable income.

[
57
]

Testimonies heard in Cross-Defence contradict
Madam Saraffian's version of the facts as to what has happened with these items
and ware.

[
58
]

Furthermore, as indicated above, no evidence has
been brought as to what Madam Saraffian was earning before Madam Kummermann
went into the hospital and what she is now earning, in order for the Court to
establish the magnitude of the loss of income.

[
59
]

There is evidence that since her mother has been
lodged, Madam Saraffian has devoted a lot of time to the various court
proceedings she has taken against her neighbour and against the Syndicate of
the property where she bought an apartment so that her mother could have lived
with her.  In those proceedings, Madam Saraffian is also claiming for loss of income
and for harassment caused by the Defendants in those cases.  Such statements
greatly decrease the probative value of the statement contained at paragraph 28
of Madam Saraffian's Cross-Demand that she has lost considerable income because
of the J.G.H.'s behaviour towards her.  Confronted with this, she states that
she has apportioned the loss between the various files.

[
60
]

The evidence reveals that, from the beginning,
Madam Saraffian refused to pay any sum whatsoever for her mother's lodging.
The J.G.H. then proceeded to take steps to have the old-age pension of her
mother paid directly to J.G.H..  Plaintiff also proceeded to notify the Public
Curator that there might be a problem with the administration of Madam
Kummermann's property, although it knew that Madam Saraffian held a Power of
Attorney.  This culminated in a hearing where the Honourable Mr. Justice Vital
Cliche dismissed the Public Curator's request to be appointed Curator to Madam
Kummermann's property.

[
61
]

The Court is of the opinion that all these
problems could have been avoided had Madam Saraffian discussed in a reasonable
and rational way with the hospital staff.  The Court has witnessed the
demeanour of Madam Kalfon, Madam Iorio and Madam Lalla who have testified as to
their dealings with Madam Saraffian.  They have also been cross-examined at
great length by Madam Saraffian who does not hesitate to twist a witness'
statements in order to have him or her contradict himself or herself.  None of
them have fallen in that trap.  All have behaved in a very calm and dignified
manner.  The Court had to call Madam Saraffian to order on a number of
occasions because the questions she put to the witnesses and the manner in
which she put them were contrary to the "Statement of principle regarding
witnesses"
[13]
and
were of such a nature as to induce the Court in error and denigrate the
administration of Justice.  None of the witnesses have lost their cool under
such difficult circumstances.

[
62
]

The Court is of the opinion that Madam Saraffian
has not discharged her burden of proving that she has lost income and that such
loss of income has been caused by the constant harassment of the different
staff members of the Plaintiff.  This is why her claim of $200,000.00 under
this heading will be dismissed.

[
63
]

V.
MOTION TO HAVE DEFENDANT, MADAM
SARAFFIAN, DECLARED A VEXATIOUS LITIGANT

[
64
]

At the beginning of the second part of the
hearing, on April 23, 2004, Plaintiff filed a Motion to have Madam Saraffian
declared a vexatious litigant pursuant to article 84 of the Rules of Practice
of the Superior Court of Quebec in Civil Matters.  Articles 84, 85 et 86 read
as follows:

84. Interdiction sauf autorisation.

Si un personne
fait preuve d'un comportement quérulent, c'est-à-dire si elle exerce son
droit d'ester en justice de manière excessive ou déraisonnable, le tribunal
peut lui interdire d'introduire une demande en justice sans autorisation
préalable.

84. Necessity to obtain prior authorization.
If a person acts in a quarrelsome
manner, that is if that person exercises litigious rights in an excessive or
unreasonable manner, the Court may prohibit that person from instituting an
action or an application without having first obtained prior judicial
authorization.

85. L'ordonnance.

L'ordonnance est générale ou limitée à un ou
plusieurs districts ou eu égard à une ou plusieurs personnes.  Dans un cas extrême
elle peut même interdire l'accès à un palais de justice.

85. The order
.  The order of prohibition is general or
is limited to one or more judicial districts, or with respect to one or more
persons.  In an extreme case, the order of prohibition may include an order
preventing the person from having access to the court-house.

86. Demande
d'autorisation.

La demande d'autorisation est adressée au juge en chef ou au juge désigné par
lui et déposée au greffe d'où origine l'ordonnance;  la demande peut être
instruite sur vue des documents, sans audience.

86. Application for authorization.
The application to institute or to continue
an action or application is presented to the Chief Justice or the judge
designated by the Chief Justice, and is filed in the Office of the Court for
the District of Quebec or the District of Montreal depending on the division
in which the order of prohibition was issued.  The application may be
adjudicated on the basis of the record, without a hearing.

[
65
]

Quarrelsome conduct or «
quérulence
» is
described as being «
une réaction revendicatrice de sujets ayant la
conviction d'être lésés.
»

[
66
]

Here is how Professor Yves-Marie Morissette (as
he then was) describes the distinctive aspects of quarrelsome conduct:

«… la quérulence dans le prétoire présente habituellement un certain
nombres de traits distinctifs, un tableau,… qui est la projection juridique
d'une attitude excessivement processive.

[…]

Premièrement, le
justiciable quérulent fait montre d'opiniâtreté et de narcissisme.  Si, dans
une société donnée pourvue d'un système de droit parvenu à pleine maturité,
chaque sujet de droit exerçait en permanence, jusqu'à la limite, la plénitude
de tous ses droits subjectifs tels qu'ils les perçoit avant procès, les
tribunaux seraient constamment sollicités par tout le monde et il est probable
que la vie en société deviendrait intolérable.  Il faut laisser du jeu au
droit, ce que la plupart des gens comprennent intuitivement et ce qui peut
expliquer, en partie du moins, l'importance relative dans le corpus litigieux
des règlements négociés avant procès.  Mais ce facteur échappe au sujet de
droit quérulent, pour qui la confrontation avec un juste contradicteur
[14]
exacerbe le sentiment d'injustice.  Toute contrariété risque donc
de se traduire de sa part par une nouvelle initiative judiciaire poursuivie
jusqu'au bout.  Deuxièmement, le justiciable quérulent se manifeste en demande
plutôt qu'en défense – et, compte tenu de l'ampleur des moyens qu'il met en
œuvre, la partie qui lui résiste risquerait elle aussi d'être taxée
d'opiniâtreté si ce n'était qu'elle est contrainte, n'ayant pas le choix des
moyens, de se défendre pied à pied.  Troisièmement, le justiciable quérulent multiplie
les recours vexatoires, y compris contre les auxiliaires de la justice.  Il
n'est pas rare, en effet, que ces procédures et ces plaintes soient dirigées
contre les avocats, le personnel judiciaire ou même les juges personnellement,
qu font l'objet d'allégations de partialité et de plaintes déontologiques.
Quatrièmement, la réitération des mêmes questions par des recours successifs et
ampliatifs, et la recherche des mêmes résultats malgré les échecs répétés de
demandes antérieures, sont fréquentes.  La partie quérulente négocie le plus
souvent à la hausse et, si elle demande des dommages-intérêts, les sommes
réclamées tendent à augmenter en cours de route et de recours en recours.
Cinquièmement, les arguments de droit mis de l'avant par le justiciable
quérulent se signalent à la fois par leur inventivité et leur incongruité.  Ils
ont une forme juridique, certes, mais sont à la limite du rationnel.  La
position prise par le demandeur dans la principale affaire
Byer
(reposant sur une lecture extravagante d'un article de la
Loi
sur les assurances
) ou par Fabrikant dans une de ses nombreuses affaires
[15]
(invoquant une loi de 1495 passée sous le règne d'Henri VIII pour
fonder un droit d'appel
in forma pauperis
) en
sont des exemples.  Sixièmement, les échecs répétés des recours ainsi exercés
par la partie quérulente entraînent à plus ou moins longue échéance son
incapacité à payer les dépens et frais de justice auxquels elle est condamnée.
On avait invoqué cette circonstance précise dans l'affaire
Grepe

v.
Loam
, première décision publiée en droit anglais où un justiciable fut
assujetti à l 'exigence d'une autorisation judiciaire préalable à l'exercice de
ses recours en justice
[16]
.  C'est une circonstance difficile à évaluer, car elle relève
plutôt de la sociologie judiciaire, mais elle mériterait d'être étudiée en
profondeur
[17]
.  Septièmement, la plupart des décisions adverses, sinon toutes,
sont portées en appel par la partie quérulente, ou font l'objet de demandes de
révision ou de rétractation.  Enfin, huitièmement, comme on l'a déjà noté, le
justiciable quérulent se représente seul.»
[18]

[
67
]

Throughout the hearing, Madam Saraffian repeated

Exhibit P-24 is the list of the various cases in

Madam Saraffian filed an Application for leave to

]

In case 500-32-042624-991

In case 500-32-048134-995

[
78
]

Madam Saraffian has given lengthy explanations
as to the nature of the various cases found in P-24.  Very often she has said
that although the case was dismissed, she is still well founded to have taken
such procedures.  The Court has the distinct impression that the fact that her
claims have been dismissed, confirmed Madam Saraffian in her thought that her

[
79
]

Infringements of her human rights, harassment,
conspiration, lack of respect towards her, lack of human values are all leitmotivs

[
80
]

The evidence is overwhelming that Madam
Saraffian «
affirme beaucoup mais prouve peu
».
[19]

[
81
]

Madam Saraffian has instituted, since 1999, many
proceedings which have all failed.  These procedures are abusive.  A litigant
is entitled to have access to the Courts but this is a right which should not
be abused.  The Administration of Justice and the adversaries of Madam
Saraffian should not be subject to unending costs and inconvenience because of
her abusive use of the Courts.  The individual adversaries and the witnesses in
the employment of the companies sued suffer great anxiety because of the behaviour
of persons like Madam Saraffian.

[
82
]

Plaintiff does not want to prevent Madam Saraffian
from having access to the Courts.  It asks that the exercise of her right to go
to Court be well-defined and supervised.  The Court has to balance Madam
Saraffian's right to have access to the Courts and the preservation of judicial
resources
[20]

especially in these days when they are becoming scarcer and scarcer.

[
83
]

In the case of
Gignac
c.
Girard
,
the honourable Mr. Justice Benoit Morin writes:

«
Si
l'accès aux tribunaux est un principe sacré dans notre société, il s'agit d'un
droit dont, comme tout autre droit, il ne faut pas abuser.  Or, le demandeur a
clairement abusé de son droit d'ester en justice et il y a lieu, en
conséquence, de baliser désormais ce droit, dans le cas du demandeur, de sorte
qu'il l'utilise à bon escient.
»
[21]

[
84
]

Considering the behaviour of Madam Saraffian
before the Court;  considering the statements made by Madam Saraffian with
respect to the cases she has been involved in since 1999;  considering the
study on quarrelsome conduct by Professor Yves-Marie Morissette (as he then
was), in the above mentioned article;  considering the best interests of the
administration of Justice, the Court is of the opinion that Madam Saraffian
acts in a quarrelsome manner because she exercises litigious rights in an
excessive and unreasonable manner;

]
